requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

task.description:
Fresh full re-review of Step 2c after implementation rework 1 (handoffs/WF02-REQ425-20260929/step-02b-mobile-dev-rework1.json describes the fix: bearer interceptor tags each request's extra with _letflowIssuedForRealm at send time; _doRefresh re-checks activeRealm.currentRealmUrl/clientId immediately after the refresh network call resolves, discarding the result on mismatch (no token write, no delete, no login routing for a tenant it no longer represents); refreshOnce/_doRefresh now return a tri-state _RefreshOutcome (success/failed/aborted); _handleUnauthorized re-checks the request's tagged realm against the current active realm immediately before reissuing the retry, throwing UnauthorizedError on any mismatch or non-success outcome). Two new regression tests added covering a tenant switch and a logout racing an in-flight 401 refresh.

Do not trust MOBILE-DEV's characterization -- read the actual current apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart yourself and independently verify the fix genuinely closes the race (not just that a check was added somewhere): confirm there is no remaining window between the realm re-check and the token write/retry where a switch could still land (e.g. is the re-check-then-act sequence itself atomic with respect to Dart's single-threaded event loop, or could another microtask interleave between the check and the write?). Re-run the full Step 2c procedure over the WHOLE diff again (INV-1..INV-8), not just the changed lines -- confirm the prior PASS verdicts (INV-4, INV-8, the three disclosed deviations) still hold on the current code, don't just assume they're unaffected. FAIL immediately, all BLOCKER, no partial credit, if anything is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: a test where the fake server returns 401 once then 200 asserts exactly one refresh call and exactly one retry, and that two concurrent requests both receiving 401 trigger one refresh total
a test where refresh fails asserts the tenant's tokens are deleted from the secure store and the router is at the login route

a test asserts a GET receiving 503 twice then 200 succeeds with increasing delays between attempts (fake clock), a GET receiving 503 on every attempt stops after the maximum attempt count declared as a named constant in lib/api/ and surfaces ApiError server (the test asserts the exact number of requests sent), and a POST receiving 503 is not retried

a test per ApiError variant asserts the mapping from status code/exception, including 404 on /api/v1/modules/exam/x -> module-not-available, 404 elsewhere -> not-found, and 429 with 'Retry-After: 7' -> backpressure(7 seconds)
a test asserts no DioException or SocketException escapes lib/api/ -- the public client API returns or throws only ApiError
the single-client guard fails its self-test fixture (a file under lib/features/ importing package:dio) and passes on the real tree
cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test pass, real output quoted, and SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off before merge

a regression test asserts that a tenant switch/logout occurring during an in-flight 401 refresh aborts the retry with a typed error rather than persisting tokens under the old realm or serving the retried request under the new tenant's identity

result.summary: INV-1 BLOCKER (new instance, not the same defect as gate_history iteration 0): the rework correctly closes the race inside _RefreshCoordinator._doRefresh (realm/clientId re-checked synchronously, with no intervening await, immediately after the refresh network call resolves and before any token write -- both new regression tests confirm zero retry requests are sent when the switch/logout happens during the refresh itself). But an equivalent, still-open race exists one step later, at retry dispatch: _handleUnauthorized's pre-retry check at api_client.dart:536 (`issuedForRealm != _activeRealm.currentRealmUrl`) runs synchronously and then calls `await _dio.fetch(retriedOptions)` with no await between the check and the fetch call -- but _dio.fetch()'s OWN internal implementation (dio 5.11.1, apps/mobile/pubspec.lock pinned version, lib/src/dio_mixin.dart:529, verified by reading the actual package source in the pub cache) builds its interceptor chain starting from `Future<dynamic> future = Future<dynamic>(() => InterceptorState(requestOptions));` -- the `Future()` constructor is documented to run its computation via Timer.run, a real event-loop turn, not a synchronous continuation and not even just a microtask. The bearer interceptor (_bearerInterceptor, api_client.dart:616) that actually attaches the retry's Authorization header only runs after this scheduled turn, and it does a FRESH, unguarded read of `activeRealm.currentRealmUrl` at that later point -- it does not consult or trust the `issuedForRealm` tag or the check _handleUnauthorized already performed. If a tenant switch/logout lands in this real, non-zero window (between _handleUnauthorized's check and the interceptor's own read), the retried request -- built from the original request issued for tenant A -- is dispatched carrying tenant B's bearer token (attached fresh by the interceptor reading the post-switch activeRealm), i.e. exactly 'serving the retried request under the new tenant's identity', which is the literal wording of this handoff's own acceptance criterion 8 and the same defect class as gate_history iteration 0, only relocated from the token-write step to the retry-dispatch step. No test in apps/mobile/test/api/api_client_hardening_test.dart exercises this window -- both new regression tests (lines 239 and 279) trigger the tenant switch/logout via `appAuthAdapter.duringRefresh`, i.e. while _doRefresh's own network await is still pending, which is caught by the earlier (correctly fixed) check at api_client.dart:254 before refreshOnce() ever returns success, so outcome never reaches _handleUnauthorized's line-536 branch in either test. The gap between the line-536 check succeeding and the bearer interceptor's fresh re-read during the scheduled retry dispatch is untested and unclosed.
issues: INV-1 BLOCKER: apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart _handleUnauthorized (line ~536) checks issuedForRealm against the current active realm before calling `_dio.fetch(retriedOptions)`, but dio 5.11.1's fetch() schedules its interceptor chain via `Future(() => ...)` (a real event-loop turn, confirmed by reading dio_mixin.dart:529 in the pinned pubspec.lock version), and the bearer interceptor that attaches the retry's Authorization header (_bearerInterceptor, line ~616) does an independent, unguarded fresh read of activeRealm.currentRealmUrl at that later point instead of trusting the pre-fetch check or the issuedForRealm tag. A tenant switch/logout landing in this window causes the retry -- built from a request issued for tenant A -- to be sent carrying tenant B's bearer token, i.e. served under the new tenant's identity. Route back to MOBILE-DEV: either re-verify the realm again inside the bearer interceptor against the request's own _kIssuedForRealmKey tag (rejecting/clearing the header if it no longer matches the currently active realm) before attaching any token to a retry, or re-check immediately before the retry response is accepted (post-fetch) and discard/abort on mismatch rather than only pre-fetch. Add a regression test that triggers the tenant switch/logout AFTER refreshOnce() resolves successfully but before the retry's interceptor chain runs (e.g. via a hook on the fake Dio adapter's send path, not appAuthAdapter.duringRefresh, since that only covers the earlier window) and asserts the retry is never sent with the new tenant's token.
result.next_action: Route back to MOBILE-DEV for rework 2: close the retry-dispatch-time realm race in _handleUnauthorized/_bearerInterceptor per issues[0], with a regression test covering the post-refresh-success, pre-retry-dispatch window specifically (distinct from the already-covered during-refresh window).

gate_history.summary: INV-1 BLOCKER: _RefreshCoordinator._doRefresh captured realmUrl before awaiting the refresh network call, allowing a concurrent tenant switch/logout to resurrect old-tenant tokens and cause a silent cross-tenant retry.
issues: _RefreshCoordinator._doRefresh/_handleUnauthorized do not re-verify the active tenant/clientId is unchanged after the async refresh completes -- untested cross-tenant race
gate_history.next_action: Route back to MOBILE-DEV (rework) to add a realm/clientId re-check before persisting refreshed tokens and before reissuing the retry, plus a regression test.
